steps.say: A mixture is two or more materials mixed together but not joined. Most mixtures can be separated again.
A sieve separates big pieces from small ones. It can separate pebbles from sand.
A filter has tiny holes. It traps insoluble bits, like sand, and lets water through.
Dissolved solids pass through a filter. To get salt back from salty water, you evaporate the water.
steps.show: salty water: evaporate the water, keep the salt

steps.say: A magnet pulls out iron and steel. It can separate iron filings from sand.

figure.alt: A magnet, an iron nail and some sand.

steps.say: Choose a method by asking what is different: the size of the pieces, dissolving or magnetism.

check.prompt: Which method gets salt back from salty water?

options.why: Dissolved salt passes through filter paper.
Dissolved salt passes straight through a sieve.

hints: The salt is dissolved in the water.
You need to get rid of the water and keep the salt.
Think about what happens to a puddle of sea water on a hot day.
check.explanation: Evaporating removes the water as water vapour. The salt is left behind as crystals.

check.prompt: Which mixture can a magnet separate?

options.why: Neither sand nor water is magnetic.
Salt is not magnetic, and it is dissolved.
Neither sugar nor flour is magnetic.

hints: A magnet only pulls on some metals.
Look for the mixture with iron in it.
check.explanation: Iron filings are magnetic and sand is not, so a magnet can pull the iron out of the sand.
